faq.q: Can a customer have several opportunities?
faq.a: Yes. Every serious buying conversation can have its own opportunity, even when several opportunities belong to the same customer.

keypoints: Knowledge Management helps customer service teams build one trusted source of knowledge instead of searching old emails, shared folders and spreadsheets.
Approved knowledge articles give consistent answers across phone, email, chat and self-service.
Teams can create, organize, review, search, publish and improve articles with answers, troubleshooting steps, procedures, policies, links and screenshots.
Knowledge is integrated into Dynamics 365 Customer Service, so agents search while working on cases without switching applications.
A good article starts with a real customer or agent problem, with clear titles, keywords, categories and plain language.
Articles should give the main answer quickly, then explain steps in order, and use terminology customers actually use.

faq.q: What is Dynamics 365 Knowledge Management?
faq.a: It is a central place to create, organize, review, search, publish and improve knowledge articles in Dynamics 365 Customer Service, giving agents approved guidance inside their case workflow.

faq.q: Why do customer service teams need a knowledge base?
faq.a: Knowledge is often scattered across documents, inboxes, shared folders and individual employees, which makes reliable answers hard to find. A shared knowledge base gives consistent answers across channels.

faq.q: How do you write an effective knowledge article?
faq.a: Start with a real problem, use clear titles, keywords, categories and simple language, give the main answer first and then the steps in order. Using customers' own terminology improves findability.

faq.q: What can a knowledge article contain?
faq.a: Answers to common questions, troubleshooting instructions, internal procedures, policies, links, screenshots and step-by-step guidance.

faq.q: How does Knowledge Management improve customer experience?
faq.a: Whether customers use phone, email, chat or self-service, agents work from the same approved information instead of inventing their own answers, which improves productivity and consistency.

keypoints: Customers who switch from website chat to phone should not have to explain their problem again; Omnichannel connects conversations across chat, voice, SMS and social messaging.
Separate systems per channel fragment the customer's story, causing repetition, longer handling times and frustrated customers.
The analogy: an office building with several front doors but one reception desk, so customers enter through many channels while agents work from one connected desk.
The unified agent workspace and customer identification bring conversations and customer history together.
Routing features include queues, Unified Routing, skills-based routing, agent presence and capacity, plus transfers and consultations.
Knowledge articles, quick replies, Copilot, Smart Assist, sentiment analysis, transcripts and supervisor analytics support agents and managers.

faq.q: What is Dynamics 365 Omnichannel?
faq.a: It is a way to connect customer conversations across chat, voice, SMS, social messaging and other service channels in a common customer service environment, so agents work from one connected desk.

faq.q: Why do separate customer service channels cause problems?
faq.a: When chats, emails, calls and social messages live in separate systems, an agent may not know the customer already chatted earlier that day. The result is repetition, longer handling times and frustrated customers.

faq.q: Does Omnichannel treat every channel the same?
faq.a: No. The channel still matters, since a live call behaves differently from an asynchronous text conversation, but agents do not necessarily need a completely separate working environment for every channel.

faq.q: How are conversations routed to agents?
faq.a: Through queues, Unified Routing and skills-based routing, taking agent presence and capacity into account, with transfers and consultations possible.

faq.q: What helps agents during a conversation?
faq.a: Knowledge articles, quick replies, Copilot, Smart Assist, sentiment analysis, customer history, cases and transcripts, while supervisors use analytics.

keypoints: An opportunity can look healthy on paper while the customer has stopped replying, so the key question is whether the customer is still talking to you.
Relationship Intelligence turns everyday communication into relationship signals in Dynamics 365 Sales, using Relationship Analytics, Relationship Health and Who Knows Whom.
Having CRM information does not mean understanding the relationship; ten activities may be nine from the salesperson with no customer response.
Activity needs context: unanswered emails or internal tasks do not equal engagement, while one conversation with the right decision-maker can matter more.
The goal is not to let Dynamics 365 decide whether a deal will close but to give sellers context about which relationship needs attention.
Signals include Exchange integration, communication activity, response times, engagement, customer sentiment, similar opportunities and warm introductions.

faq.q: What is Dynamics 365 Relationship Intelligence?
faq.a: It turns everyday customer communication, such as emails and meetings, into relationship signals in Dynamics 365 Sales, helping sellers see whether a customer relationship is active or has gone quiet.

faq.q: Why can a CRM record look active when the relationship is quiet?
faq.a: Because activity is not engagement. A record may show many emails and tasks, yet most come from the salesperson, the customer has stopped replying and no future meeting is scheduled.

faq.q: What does Who Knows Whom do?
faq.a: It addresses the case where another employee already knows an important decision-maker but the salesperson does not know the relationship exists, supporting warm introductions.

faq.q: Does Relationship Intelligence predict whether a deal will close?
faq.a: No. The goal is not to decide whether a deal will close but to give sellers better context for deciding which relationship needs attention and what conversation should happen next.

faq.q: Which signals does Relationship Intelligence use?
faq.a: Communication activity from Microsoft Exchange integration, response times, engagement, customer sentiment and similar opportunities, supporting opportunity management and pipeline prioritization.

keypoints: Dynamics 365 Forecasting helps sales teams answer whether they will hit the sales target, using opportunity data already in Dynamics 365 Sales.
A sales forecast is not a guarantee but a continuously changing estimate based on what the sales organization currently knows.
The forecast combines expected deal value, close dates, quotas, ownership and confidence.
Shared forecasts replace individual spreadsheets that sellers update at different times and managers must consolidate.
The forecast grid works like a shared scorecard, with rows for sellers, teams, territories or products, and columns for quota, forecast amounts and confidence levels.
Forecast categories give a common language for confidence, and accurate opportunity data is essential for reliable forecasts.

faq.q: What is Dynamics 365 Forecasting?
faq.a: It turns the opportunities a sales team already manages in Dynamics 365 Sales into a structured view of expected revenue, combining opportunities, close dates, forecast categories, quotas and sales performance.

faq.q: Is a sales forecast a guarantee of revenue?
faq.a: No. It is a continuously changing estimate based on what the organization currently knows about its open opportunities, showing both potential revenue and how realistic it is for the period.

faq.q: What is the forecast grid?
faq.a: A shared sales scorecard. Rows can represent sellers, teams, territories or products and columns can show quota, forecast amounts and confidence levels, letting managers drill into the opportunities behind totals.

faq.q: What are forecast categories?
faq.a: They provide a common language for describing the confidence behind each opportunity, starting with Pipeline at the lower end of confidence.

faq.q: Why does opportunity data quality matter for forecasting?
faq.a: The forecast is built from opportunity data, so inaccurate values or close dates lead to unreliable revenue forecasts.

keypoints: Agents need the complete customer story quickly, but without a unified workspace that means jumping between tabs, inboxes, CRM records, notes and knowledge bases.
Customer Service Workspace is now known as Copilot Service Workspace, so both names may appear in documentation and training.
Think of it as a browser designed around customer service, organizing related information around the piece of customer work being handled.
The aim is not just to show CRM records but to let agents switch between customer issues without losing and rebuilding context.
Agents juggle several customers and channels, such as a call, a new high-priority email and a case near its response deadline.
The workspace covers sessions and tabs, cases and timelines, Smart Assist, knowledge, scripts, macros, quick replies, Copilot, Teams, routing, SLAs and analytics.

faq.q: What is Dynamics 365 Customer Service Workspace?
faq.a: It is a focused working environment for customer service agents that keeps the customer, the problem, the history, the knowledge and the tools needed to solve it connected in one organized workspace.

faq.q: Is Customer Service Workspace the same as Copilot Service Workspace?
faq.a: Microsoft now refers to this newer agent experience as Copilot Service Workspace, so organizations may see both names in documentation, videos, training materials or existing environments.

faq.q: Why do customer service agents need a different workspace?
faq.a: Agents handle several customers and channels at once. Without a unified workspace, answering what the customer owns, whether a case exists or what was promised requires hopping between many applications.

faq.q: What does the workspace include?
faq.a: Sessions and tabs, cases and timelines, omnichannel service, the agent inbox, Smart Assist, knowledge management, agent scripts, macros, quick replies, Copilot, Teams collaboration, routing, SLA management and dashboards.

faq.q: How do sessions and tabs help agents?
faq.a: They organize related information around the customer work currently being handled, so agents can move between issues without repeatedly losing and rebuilding context.

keypoints: Integration has become infrastructure; like turning on a water tap, its complexity stays invisible until something fails.
Integration is not just connecting application A with B but keeping business processes running across systems never designed to work together.
Traditional integration is deterministic: triggers, conditions, transformations, retries and exceptions are defined in advance.
Sonny Gillissen's concept Organism as a Service describes integration that interprets context, responds to unexpected situations, chooses actions and recovers from failures more intelligently.
The conversation covers Azure Logic Apps, API Management, Functions, Service Bus, Event Grid, managed identities, Key Vault, Bicep, Terraform, CI/CD and observability.
It also addresses security with least privilege and network isolation, AI agent loops and self-healing integrations.

faq.q: What is Organism as a Service in enterprise integration?
faq.a: It is Sonny Gillissen's idea that integration can evolve from static workflows into systems that interpret context, respond to unexpected situations, choose appropriate actions and potentially recover from failures more intelligently.

faq.q: How does AI change Azure Logic Apps integrations?
faq.a: Integration has been deterministic: when this happens, do that. With AI in the integration layer, workflows can use agent loops to handle unexpected situations and move toward self-healing integrations.

faq.q: Why does enterprise integration matter?
faq.a: Applications, APIs, ERP systems and data must work together reliably. Employees and customers expect information and orders to reach the right systems automatically, like water from a tap.

faq.q: Which Azure services does the episode cover?
faq.a: Azure Logic Apps, Azure Integration Services, API Management, Azure Functions, Service Bus, Event Grid, managed connectors, managed identities, Key Vault and Log Analytics.

faq.q: What practices does the episode link to production integrations?
faq.a: Infrastructure as Code with Bicep and Terraform, CI/CD, observability, least privilege and network isolation.

keypoints: When a machine stops, the technician sees the problem but the expert may be far away, and expertise is hard to bring to where the work happens.
Remote Assist connects frontline workers with remote experts through live video, visual guidance, Microsoft Teams, mobile devices and mixed reality.
Central idea: instead of describing a physical problem to someone who cannot see it, let the expert see what the frontline worker sees.
Phone support forces technicians to translate a physical situation into words, which invites misunderstanding, such as which connector is meant.
It supports field service, manufacturing, maintenance, inspections, troubleshooting, training and remote collaboration.
It connects with Dynamics 365 Field Service and Microsoft 365 identity and security.

faq.q: What is Dynamics 365 Remote Assist?
faq.a: It lets frontline workers connect with remote experts through live video and visual guidance, using Microsoft Teams, mobile devices or mixed reality, so the expert sees what the worker sees.

faq.q: Why is phone support limited for technical problems?
faq.a: The technician must translate a physical situation into words. A remark like something is wrong with the connector at the back leaves open which connector, which side and whether there is damage.

faq.q: Which jobs benefit from Remote Assist?
faq.a: Field service, manufacturing, maintenance, inspections, troubleshooting and training, where employees work beside equipment or at customer sites far from a desk.

faq.q: How does Remote Assist relate to Teams and Field Service?
faq.a: It uses Microsoft Teams for remote collaboration and connects with Dynamics 365 Field Service processes, within Microsoft 365 identity and security.

faq.q: What problem does Remote Assist solve besides missing expertise?
faq.a: The challenge is not that expertise does not exist but getting it to the place of work without repeated questions, photos or sending a specialist to the site.

keypoints: Unified Routing is an intelligent capability that automatically distributes incoming customer service work to appropriate agents.
It classifies incoming requests, determines priority, identifies required skills, considers agent availability and workload, and routes work to the most appropriate person.
The analogy is a smart front desk that understands each visitor's needs instead of sending everyone to the same waiting room.
A shared inbox that works for five agents becomes a bottleneck with many channels, languages, priorities and technical skill requirements.
Explains workstreams, queues, skills, capacity profiles, presence, push assignment, pick assignment, machine learning and fallback queues.
Unified Routing works with Copilot Service workspace.

faq.q: What is Dynamics 365 Unified Routing?
faq.a: It is an intelligent routing capability that distributes incoming customer service work to appropriate agents. It asks not just which agent is next but who has the skills, who is available, how much work each has and how urgent the request is.

faq.q: Why do basic customer service queues stop working?
faq.a: A single shared queue works for a few agents with one product and language. As requests arrive through email, chat, voice, messaging and web forms with different topics, languages and priorities, it becomes a bottleneck.

faq.q: What does Unified Routing take into account?
faq.a: The customer's need, required skills, priority, agent availability, presence and current workload or capacity.

faq.q: What is the difference between push and pick assignment?
faq.a: The episode covers both as assignment methods in Unified Routing. In push assignment the system assigns work to agents, while in pick assignment agents take items from a queue.

faq.q: What are fallback queues for?
faq.a: They are part of the routing setup discussed in the episode, alongside workstreams, queues, skills and capacity profiles, to handle work that no rule matches.

keypoints: Dynamics 365 Guides is a Microsoft mixed reality application that brought step-by-step work instructions into the physical environment where tasks are done.
Through a HoloLens headset it showed instruction cards, images, videos and 3D objects while the employee still saw the real machine and tools.
The fundamental concept: bring the instruction to the work instead of forcing the worker to leave the work to find the instruction.
Typical scenarios are manufacturing, maintenance, inspections, field service, training and assembly.
Companies could capture expert knowledge, and Teams enabled remote assistance.
Microsoft has set December 31, 2026 as the end-of-availability date for Dynamics 365 Guides and Dynamics 365 Remote Assist, so preserving existing Guides content matters.

faq.q: What is Dynamics 365 Guides?
faq.a: It is a Microsoft mixed reality application that displays step-by-step work instructions, images, videos and 3D objects through a HoloLens headset directly in the physical workplace.

faq.q: What problem did Dynamics 365 Guides solve?
faq.a: Physical work often happens far from the information needed to perform it. Technicians, operators and inspectors had to walk back to a laptop or search PDFs; Guides placed the instructions in their field of view.

faq.q: When does Dynamics 365 Guides reach end of availability?
faq.a: Microsoft has set December 31, 2026 as the end-of-availability date for Dynamics 365 Guides and Dynamics 365 Remote Assist.

faq.q: What should organizations do about the end of Guides?
faq.a: The episode says organizations still using the technology should preserve the knowledge contained in their Guides, which is becoming as important as understanding the technology itself.

faq.q: Where was Dynamics 365 Guides used?
faq.a: In manufacturing, maintenance, inspections, field service, training, assembly and other repeatable physical processes.

keypoints: Sales teams rarely lack data; the problem is knowing which information matters now and what to do next, and follow-ups get lost.
Sales Insights is a collection of AI-powered capabilities that make information in Dynamics 365 Sales more actionable, on top of the CRM foundation.
It looks for signals such as overdue activities, leads resembling previously converted leads or declining communication with an important account.
The objective is not more data but better guidance from the data the sales organization already has.
Without it, answers about which opportunities will close depend on memory and intuition, with notes, spreadsheets and reminders spread across tools.
Covers Auto Capture, Email Engagement, predictive scoring, Sales Accelerator, relationship intelligence, Conversation Intelligence and LinkedIn Sales Navigator.

faq.q: What is Dynamics 365 Sales Insights?
faq.a: It is a collection of AI and intelligence capabilities that sit on top of Dynamics 365 Sales and surface useful signals, so sellers need not search thousands of records manually.

faq.q: Why do sales teams need insights rather than more data?
faq.a: Sales generates enormous amounts of information in CRM records, emails, meetings and notes. The difficulty is knowing which matters right now, otherwise forecasts rely on memory and intuition.

faq.q: What features belong to Sales Insights?
faq.a: The assistant, Auto Capture, Email Engagement, predictive lead and opportunity scoring, Sales Accelerator, relationship intelligence, Who Knows Whom, Talking Points, Conversation Intelligence, notes analysis and forecasting.

faq.q: What kind of signals can Sales Insights find?
faq.a: An important activity may be overdue, a lead may resemble previously converted leads, communication with an important account may have declined, or an opportunity may show patterns of earlier successful deals.

faq.q: Which integrations does the episode mention?
faq.a: The episode mentions Microsoft 365, Microsoft Teams and LinkedIn Sales Navigator as integrations. They connect Sales Insights with the tools sellers already use, so relevant information can come closer to their daily work.

keypoints: Salespeople struggle less with too few tasks than with deciding which customer deserves attention next and what to do.
Sales Accelerator is a guided selling experience inside Dynamics 365 Sales and does not replace it.
It acts as the seller's daily desk, answering who to work with today and what to do next, bringing together leads, opportunities, activities, suggested actions and customer context.
Sales work is fragmented across Outlook, the calendar, phone, spreadsheets and CRM lists, and a busy day can still miss key opportunities.
Features include Up Next, the work list, sequences for repeatable steps, predictive scoring and Outlook integration.
Explains where automation helps and where human judgment remains essential.

faq.q: What is Dynamics 365 Sales Accelerator?
faq.a: It is a guided selling experience inside Dynamics 365 Sales that helps sellers prioritize leads and opportunities, organize daily activities and keep customer context close to every interaction.

faq.q: Does Sales Accelerator replace Dynamics 365 Sales?
faq.a: No. Dynamics 365 Sales remains the larger CRM with accounts, contacts, leads, opportunities and history, and Sales Accelerator provides a more focused working experience on top.

faq.q: What are sequences in Sales Accelerator?
faq.a: Sequences are repeatable sales steps that help organize daily activities so that follow-ups happen in a consistent way.

faq.q: What question does Sales Accelerator answer?
faq.a: It answers the practical question every seller faces: who should I work with today, and what should I do next, based on leads, opportunities, activities and customer context.

faq.q: Where does human judgment remain essential?
faq.a: The episode points out that automation and guided selling help with prioritization, while sellers still need judgment about how to approach customers.

keypoints: Dynamics 365 Human Resources is a cloud-based HR solution giving organizations a central place for employee information and common HR processes.
HR data such as employee records, leave, benefits, compensation, skills, certifications and performance is sensitive and must be accurate and accessible to the right people.
Information spread across spreadsheets, emails and disconnected systems goes out of date with every extra copy of the employee record.
Requests can follow predefined approval processes, managers see their teams and employees use self-service.
The goal is not one application for everything; payroll, recruitment or learning can remain specialized solutions that rely on the central people information.
Topics include onboarding, learning and development, workflows, automation, reporting, Teams, Power BI and payroll integrations.

faq.q: What is Dynamics 365 Human Resources?
faq.a: It is a cloud-based HR solution that provides a central place for employee information and common HR processes, built around a shared employee record.

faq.q: Why is fragmented HR data a problem?
faq.a: When a new employee joins, data may be entered in HR, a manager's list, payroll and training systems. Every extra copy can become outdated, for example when an employee changes departments.

faq.q: Does it replace payroll and recruitment tools?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Organizations may still use specialized solutions for payroll, recruitment or learning; Dynamics 365 Human Resources supplies the central people information they depend on.

faq.q: What is employee and manager self-service?
faq.a: Employees can perform appropriate self-service activities and managers can access information about their teams, while requests follow predefined approval processes.

faq.q: Which HR processes does the episode cover?
faq.a: Employee records, organizational structures, leave and absence, benefits, compensation, learning and development, onboarding, workflows, automation and reporting.

keypoints: Azure SQL Database provides familiar SQL Server relational capabilities while removing much of the infrastructure management of running a production database.
Dirceu Resende argues that a database can become an active participant in application architecture instead of waiting passively for applications.
Azure SQL Database can make HTTP requests and talk to external services, letting it take part in workflows that once needed another integration layer.
Azure SQL Managed Instance is closer to traditional SQL Server and suits migrations of existing workloads, while Azure SQL Database fits independent databases and microservices.
The conversation covers REST API integration, automation, security, performance, Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, AI, vector search, RAG and observability.
Dirceu has a background in database development, performance tuning and business intelligence, and previously worked at Microsoft as a Senior Program Manager for Power BI.

faq.q: Is Azure SQL Database more than a place to store data?
faq.a: Yes, according to Dirceu Resende. Beyond tables and transactions, Azure SQL Database can make HTTP requests and communicate with external services, so the database can take part in workflows directly.

faq.q: What is the difference between Azure SQL Database and Managed Instance?
faq.a: Managed Instance gives an experience closer to traditional SQL Server, supporting multiple databases within an instance and features useful for migrations. Azure SQL Database suits independent databases and microservice architectures.

faq.q: What does Azure SQL Database take off your hands?
faq.a: Much of the infrastructure management, since organizations use a managed cloud database without maintaining the underlying operating system, while Azure adds security, availability, backups, performance and integration.

faq.q: Which AI topics does the episode cover for Azure SQL?
faq.a: The episode covers AI, vector search and RAG in connection with Azure SQL. It also touches Microsoft Fabric, Power BI and observability as part of the discussion about the changing role of databases in modern applications.

faq.q: Who is Dirceu Resende?
faq.a: He is a database and business intelligence expert whose career spans database development, performance tuning, Power BI and cloud technologies, including work at Microsoft as a Senior Program Manager for Power BI.

keypoints: The same customer appears in sales, service, marketing and order systems, each telling a different story, so nobody sees the complete picture.
Dynamics 365 Customer Insights - Data is Microsoft's Customer Data Platform (CDP), which connects information from existing systems instead of replacing CRM, sales, service or marketing apps.
A CDP brings data from approved sources together, identifies records that appear to be the same customer and creates unified customer profiles.
Scattered data leads to bad decisions: sales approaching a customer with a serious support problem, or marketing promoting an upgrade to someone who just bought.
Covers unifying records, 360-degree profiles, measures, segments, AI-powered predictions and activating insights across Microsoft business applications.

faq.q: What is Dynamics 365 Customer Insights - Data?
faq.a: It is Microsoft's Customer Data Platform (CDP). It connects customer information from different systems, unifies matching records into profiles and makes them usable by other business processes.

faq.q: Does Customer Insights - Data replace CRM or marketing applications?
faq.a: No. Its purpose is to connect information from those systems to create a more complete understanding of each customer rather than to replace them.

faq.q: Why does scattered customer data cause problems?
faq.a: Each system holds a useful perspective but not the whole story, so sales may approach a customer with a support problem, or marketing may promote an upgrade to someone who just purchased.

faq.q: What is a unified customer profile?
faq.a: A profile created when the CDP identifies records from different sources that appear to represent the same customer and combines them into a 360-degree view.

faq.q: What can organizations do with the unified data?
faq.a: Calculate measures, build segments, use AI-powered predictions and activate customer insights across Microsoft business applications.

keypoints: A customer who finds a jacket online, orders it for pickup and returns it elsewhere expects one journey, though it touches e-commerce, point of sale, inventory, pricing, payments and returns.
Dynamics 365 Commerce is Microsoft's platform connecting the processes of selling across physical stores, websites and other channels.
Without shared data a website may show a different price than a store, show unavailable items as available, or hide web orders from store staff.
It is much more than an e-commerce website builder or point-of-sale application.
Commerce evolved from Dynamics 365 Retail, which focused on physical retail and point of sale.
In omnichannel retail, customers move between channels while business information stays connected, and channels are entrances to the same operation.

faq.q: What is Dynamics 365 Commerce?
faq.a: It is Microsoft's platform for connecting the processes behind selling products across physical stores, websites and other commerce channels, covering products, inventory, pricing, customers, orders, loyalty and fulfillment.

faq.q: How is Dynamics 365 Commerce related to Dynamics 365 Retail?
faq.a: Commerce evolved from Retail, which primarily focused on physical retail operations and point of sale. Commerce reflects shopping journeys that no longer remain in a single channel.

faq.q: What does omnichannel retail mean?
faq.a: Customers can move between channels, such as starting on a smartphone and finishing in a store, while the underlying business information stays connected.

faq.q: What problems appear when retail systems are separate?
faq.a: A website might show a different price than the store, a product could look available online while stock is missing, and store employees may be unable to access a web order.

faq.q: Is Dynamics 365 Commerce just a web shop?
faq.a: No. It is a connected foundation for stores, e-commerce, point of sale and back-office retail operations, not merely a website builder.

keypoints: Dynamics 365 Project Operations is designed for organizations that sell project-based services such as consulting, engineering or implementation work.
It connects project sales, project management, resource planning, time tracking, expenses, billing and financial processes on one platform.
Without it, sales, delivery, time recording and finance each hold their own version of the project, and finance struggles to determine what to invoice.
The goal is not one interface for everyone but keeping the underlying project information connected across roles.
During the sales process, needs, roles, hours, start dates, cost and billing can be captured to link what sales promises with what delivery must provide.
Follows the lifecycle from first conversation and quote through planning, staffing, delivery, time and expense, financial tracking and invoicing.

faq.q: What is Dynamics 365 Project Operations?
faq.a: It is a platform for organizations that sell project-based services, connecting people, time, costs, contracts and billing from the sales quote through delivery to customer invoicing.

faq.q: What problem does Project Operations solve?
faq.a: Departments often create separate versions of a project: sales knows what was promised, delivery has another plan, hours are recorded elsewhere, and finance later tries to work out what belongs on the invoice.

faq.q: How does Project Operations connect sales and delivery?
faq.a: While the opportunity is still developing, it captures needs, roles, hours, start dates, cost and billing, which links what sales promises with what the delivery organization must provide.

faq.q: Who uses Project Operations?
faq.a: Salespeople, consultants, project managers, resource managers and finance professionals, each with different responsibilities but shared project information.

faq.q: What parts of the project lifecycle does the episode follow?
faq.a: The first sales conversation and quote, planning, staffing, delivery, time and expense management, financial tracking and finally customer invoicing.

keypoints: Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management is a cloud-based ERP solution for managing the physical movement of products and materials.
It connects what a company buys, has in stock, can manufacture, where products are stored and how they reach customers.
It should not be viewed as just warehouse management software, since it spans product information, procurement, production, transportation and fulfillment.
The central idea is a connected operational view instead of disconnected spreadsheets, reports, emails and manual handoffs.
Every supply chain begins with reliable product information; Product Information Management provides shared product records with names, dimensions, weights, units and variations.
The journey covers demand forecasting, procurement, inventory, warehouse, manufacturing, asset management, transportation, analytics and AI.

faq.q: What is Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management?
faq.a: It is a cloud-based enterprise resource planning solution that helps organizations manage the physical movement of products and materials through suppliers, warehouses, factories, carriers and customers.

faq.q: Is Supply Chain Management only warehouse software?
faq.a: No. Warehouse operations are an important component, but the platform covers product information, procurement, production, transportation and final fulfillment.

faq.q: Why does product information matter in a supply chain?
faq.a: Every supply chain begins with reliable product records. A material may be bought by the kilogram, stored in boxes and sold individually, so consistent names, units, dimensions and variations are required.

faq.q: What does connected operational view mean here?
faq.a: Changes in inventory, expected deliveries, production schedules or shipments become part of a shared picture, rather than separate versions kept by purchasing, warehouse, production and customer service.

faq.q: Which areas does the episode walk through?
faq.a: Product records, demand forecasting, procurement, inventory, warehouse operations, manufacturing, asset management, transportation, fulfillment, analytics, AI and customer delivery.

keypoints: A simple question such as how much can we spend this month becomes slow when spreadsheets, bank balances, approvals and sales numbers sit in different places.
Dynamics 365 Finance is Microsoft's system for recording, tracking, controlling and reporting money moving through an organization.
Almost everything departments do creates a financial consequence: a sale creates revenue, a purchase a cost, supplier and customer invoices money owed or expected.
With a shared platform, the transaction itself is the official record instead of another spreadsheet copy.
Using Dynamics 365 Finance does not mean abandoning Excel, which stays useful for exploration, models and analysis.
Runs from the first purchase request through the general ledger, budgeting, reporting, security and the wider Microsoft platform.

faq.q: What is Dynamics 365 Finance?
faq.a: It is Microsoft's system for recording, tracking, controlling and reporting money moving through an organization, covering transactions, purchasing, supplier payments, budgets, forecasts, cash and financial reports.

faq.q: What does one financial source of truth mean?
faq.a: Without a shared platform, invoices are re-entered in other applications and budgets sit in Excel. Dynamics 365 Finance makes the transaction itself the official record, reducing wrong, missing or duplicate entries.

faq.q: Can you still use Excel with Dynamics 365 Finance?
faq.a: Yes. Excel remains useful for exploring information, building models, investigating questions and analysis.

faq.q: Why does Finance sit at the center of a company?
faq.a: Almost everything other departments do creates a financial consequence, so Finance connects those activities with the company's official financial records.

faq.q: Which topics does the Finance episode cover?
faq.a: The path from the first purchase request through the general ledger, budgeting, reporting, security and the wider Microsoft platform.

keypoints: Microsoft 365 can start like a garage band, but growth brings multiplying Teams, accumulating SharePoint sites, lingering guests, inconsistent naming and unclear ownership.
Heiko Brenn sees governance as the balance between creativity, freedom and structure, working unobtrusively in the background.
Governance should enable collaboration rather than restrict it, and it is not bureaucracy for its own sake.
Governance, security, administration and compliance are not the same: security provides foundations like MFA, while governance reflects how people and departments work.
Finance, HR, Legal, Sales, Development and Marketing may need different policies because information, risks, processes and regulations differ.
Heiko is Director of Product Marketing at BCC with more than 30 years of IT experience.

faq.q: What is Microsoft 365 governance about?
faq.a: According to Heiko Brenn, it is about balancing freedom and structure: employees stay creative and productive while the necessary rules and processes work unobtrusively in the background.

faq.q: How does governance differ from security?
faq.a: Security provides foundational protections such as MFA and other technical measures. Governance sits above and translates organizational requirements into practical rules that fit how people and departments work.

faq.q: Why does Microsoft 365 need governance as it grows?
faq.a: Teams multiply, SharePoint sites accumulate, guests stay after projects end, naming becomes inconsistent, ownership is unclear and manual administration cannot keep pace.

faq.q: Should every department have the same governance rules?
faq.a: No. Finance, HR, Legal, Sales, Development and Marketing have different information, risks, processes and regulatory requirements and may need different policies.

faq.q: Who is Heiko Brenn?
faq.a: Director of Product Marketing at BCC, with over 30 years of IT experience in administration, consulting, Exchange, PowerShell, product management and Microsoft 365 governance.

keypoints: Repeating your story to a chat bot, a phone agent and a transferred agent is a systems problem, not a customer problem.
Dynamics 365 Contact Center is Microsoft's cloud service for managing live customer conversations across voice and digital channels from a connected workspace.
A modern contact center manages conversations, not only calls: phone, web chat, text, email, mobile apps and social messaging reach the right people from a common environment.
It is not the same as CRM: the CRM is the long-term customer filing cabinet, while Contact Center is the service desk handling the live interaction.
Covers routing, customer context, Copilot, AI agents, supervisors and existing CRM systems.

faq.q: What is Dynamics 365 Contact Center?
faq.a: It is Microsoft's cloud service for managing live customer conversations across voice and digital channels from a connected workspace, bringing voice, chat, messaging, routing and customer context together.

faq.q: How is a contact center different from a phone system?
faq.a: A phone system mainly manages calls. A modern contact center manages customer conversations across phone, chat, text, email and social channels, deciding where each goes and giving agents the tools to respond.

faq.q: Is Dynamics 365 Contact Center the same as CRM?
faq.a: No. The CRM holds the broader, long-term customer story such as purchases, cases and service history, while the Contact Center focuses on the live interaction in front of that filing cabinet.

faq.q: Why do customers have to repeat their story across channels?
faq.a: Because channels run on disconnected systems. Connecting them in one environment lets context follow the customer from chat to phone or a transfer.

faq.q: Which technologies does the episode combine?
faq.a: Voice, chat, messaging, routing, customer context, Copilot, AI agents, supervisors and existing CRM systems.

keypoints: Customer Insights - Journeys is more than a marketing email tool: it connects customer information, communication, customer actions and business processes.
Disconnected systems produce disconnected communication, such as generic emails, repeated demo invitations or a salesperson calling someone who already submitted a detailed request.
Customers experience one company, not separate departments, so communication should follow the customer's situation rather than a department's campaign.
The objective is not sending more messages but determining the next sensible message, who should hear from you and when.
A website visitor who downloads a product guide can get related information instead of a generic monthly mailing, and sales gains context from the interaction.

faq.q: What is Dynamics 365 Customer Insights - Journeys?
faq.a: It is a system that connects customer information, communication, customer actions and business processes so organizations can decide who should hear from them, what message to send and when.

faq.q: Is Customer Insights - Journeys just an email tool?
faq.a: No. The episode presents it as something larger than marketing email: a connected system for planning customer communication around the customer's situation across Marketing, Sales and Service.

faq.q: What is the next sensible message?
faq.a: Instead of putting everyone on a generic mailing list, the business responds to what a person did, such as downloading a guide on a product, with related information.

faq.q: What problems does disconnected communication cause?
faq.a: Customers get irrelevant mail, prospects who booked a demo get asked to book again, and salespeople call people without knowing their earlier request.

faq.q: How does Journeys help sales?
faq.a: Sales gains context from the customer's earlier interactions, so the conversation does not start without knowing what the person has already done.

keypoints: Sales, Service, Marketing and website systems each hold part of the customer relationship, so employees rarely see the whole history.
Customer Insights helps organizations understand customers and use that understanding for more relevant communication.
It has two parts: Customer Insights - Data, which brings information together, and Customer Insights - Journeys, which plans and delivers communication.
A simple way to remember: Data helps you see the customer, Journeys helps you respond to the customer.
Naming changes make the product look more complicated than it is; the episode explains the naming history from before September 2023.
Follows data from disconnected records through unified profiles, segments, journeys, triggers, personalization, consent, analytics and human follow-up.

faq.q: What is Dynamics 365 Customer Insights?
faq.a: It helps organizations understand customers by bringing fragmented information together and then use that understanding to communicate in a more relevant way. It consists of Customer Insights - Data and Customer Insights - Journeys.

faq.q: What is the difference between Customer Insights - Data and Journeys?
faq.a: Data brings information together and helps organizations see the customer. Journeys uses customer information to plan and deliver communications based on who someone is and what they do.

faq.q: Why is customer data fragmented?
faq.a: Each interaction lands somewhere different: Sales holds the opportunity, Service the case, ecommerce the purchases, the website form submissions and marketing systems the emails, leaving one customer with several disconnected versions.

faq.q: Why is the Customer Insights name confusing?
faq.a: Microsoft's naming changes made it seem more complex; the episode explains the history from before September 2023.

faq.q: What role do consent and human follow-up play?
faq.a: They are part of the flow the episode follows from unified profiles and segments to journeys, triggers and personalization, with consent, analytics and people following up.

keypoints: A repair request needs more than sending someone: a technician who is nearby, available, qualified for the equipment and ideally carrying the replacement part.
Dynamics 365 Field Service connects service requests, scheduling, dispatch, mobile field work, inventory, asset management, maintenance and billing into one process.
Field service means work performed at a customer location, such as repairing air conditioning, inspecting hospital equipment or responding to outages.
First-visit resolution requires the right technician, the right information and the right parts.
Without a shared platform dispatchers reconstruct availability, equipment data and repair history from calendars, spreadsheets and emails.
Field Service and Customer Service solve related but different parts of the customer journey.

faq.q: What is Dynamics 365 Field Service?
faq.a: It is a platform that connects customer information, service jobs, technicians, schedules, equipment and service details so work performed at customer locations can be planned, dispatched, completed and billed.

faq.q: Why does first-visit resolution matter?
faq.a: Customers do not want to wait for a late technician or discover the required part is missing. A first-visit fix needs the right technician, information and parts.

faq.q: What do dispatchers need to decide?
faq.a: Who is available, who is nearby, who has the right skills and whether the technician can reach the customer within the promised window, ideally from current data rather than phone calls and memory.

faq.q: What does a technician need in the field?
faq.a: The complete service history and clear instructions, while the office needs to know what happened and turn completed work into an accurate invoice.

faq.q: What is the difference between Field Service and Customer Service?
faq.a: They are related but solve different parts of the customer journey; Customer Service handles requests and cases while Field Service handles work at the customer's site.

keypoints: Microsoft 365 data moves between Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, Fabric and Excel files, being copied, renamed, shared and sometimes forgotten.
Microsoft Purview helps organizations find, understand, protect, govern and manage data, and the Data Map is a foundation for making enterprise information understandable and trustworthy.
Data sprawl grows with new applications, spreadsheets, file shares and cloud services, and mergers and acquisitions make it larger.
Organizations may have hundreds or thousands of information locations without a complete directory of what exists.
When nobody knows which data to trust, an analyst may pick the newest of five similar pricing spreadsheets and the numbers later do not match the official data.
Secure identities, endpoints and applications do not automatically mean secure data.

faq.q: What is the Microsoft Purview Data Map?
faq.a: It is described as an important foundation of Microsoft Purview for making enterprise information understandable and trustworthy, helping organizations find, understand and govern data across locations.

faq.q: Why does data sprawl become a business problem?
faq.a: It affects decisions: with many similar spreadsheets, people cannot tell which data is authoritative, who owns it or where it came from, so reports may not match official figures.

faq.q: Does secure infrastructure mean secure data?
faq.a: No. Organizations can have secure identities, endpoints and applications and still face serious information risks because data keeps moving and being copied.

faq.q: How does data sprawl arise?
faq.a: As teams add applications, databases, spreadsheets, reports, file shares and cloud services; mergers keep old systems running; and reports are exported, emailed and stored elsewhere.

faq.q: What does Microsoft Purview help organizations do?
faq.a: Microsoft Purview helps organizations find, understand, protect, govern and manage their data as it moves across Microsoft 365 and other locations.

keypoints: Microsoft Entra Connect is widely known but often misunderstood; the episode explains why organizations need it and what gets synchronized between Active Directory and Entra ID.
Hybrid identity exists because companies managed identities in on-premises Active Directory while Microsoft 365 needed its own cloud identity system, Microsoft Entra ID.
Active Directory is the local records room and Entra ID is the cloud reception desk; Entra Connect is the controlled bridge between them.
Without synchronization IT would maintain a second identity per employee manually, so changes like a department could differ between systems.
Breaks Entra Connect into synchronization, authentication and health monitoring, including where passwords are checked and what happens if synchronization stops.

faq.q: What is Microsoft Entra Connect?
faq.a: It is the controlled bridge between on-premises Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID in a hybrid identity environment, so both systems represent the same employees instead of becoming two disconnected directories.

faq.q: Why do organizations need Entra Connect?
faq.a: Microsoft 365 needs a cloud identity in Entra ID while many companies keep Active Directory. Without synchronization IT would create and maintain every identity twice by hand.

faq.q: What is hybrid identity?
faq.a: A setup in which an organization uses both on-premises Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID for its employees.

faq.q: What are the building blocks of Entra Connect?
faq.a: The episode breaks Microsoft Entra Connect into three building blocks: synchronization of identities, authentication, and health monitoring of the connection.

faq.q: What is the difference between Active Directory and Entra ID?
faq.a: Active Directory holds employee identities, groups and access information for the corporate network; Entra ID identifies employees accessing Teams, Exchange Online, SharePoint, OneDrive and other cloud services.

keypoints: Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync is a cloud-managed way to synchronize identities from on-premises Active Directory into Microsoft Entra ID.
Without synchronization IT maintains two identity environments, which matters when employees join, change departments, get new permissions, change passwords or leave.
Entra Connect runs a synchronization engine inside the organization's network; it is flexible but the server must be maintained, patched, monitored and covered by disaster recovery.
If Entra Connect's infrastructure is unavailable, changes may stop reaching Microsoft 365, affecting new and departing employees, permissions and password changes.
Cloud Sync moves much of the processing into Microsoft Entra in the cloud, with a lightweight provisioning agent remaining on premises.
Covers architecture, high availability, scoping, security, hybrid environments, the decision between Cloud Sync and Entra Connect and what has changed in 2026.

faq.q: What is Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync?
faq.a: It is a cloud-managed way to synchronize identities from on-premises Active Directory into Microsoft Entra ID. More of the processing is handled in the cloud, with a lightweight provisioning agent inside the organization.

faq.q: How is Entra Cloud Sync different from Entra Connect?
faq.a: Entra Connect runs a full synchronization engine inside the company network and brings operational responsibility. Cloud Sync shifts much of the work to Microsoft Entra in the cloud.

faq.q: Why does identity synchronization still matter?
faq.a: Many organizations keep identities in Active Directory while employees work in Microsoft 365. Synchronization lets changes flow from the local directory to Entra ID instead of maintaining two accounts.

faq.q: What risks come with an on-premises synchronization server?
faq.a: It must be maintained, patched, monitored and included in disaster recovery planning, and if it becomes unavailable, identity changes may stop reaching Microsoft 365.

faq.q: Which topics does the episode cover when choosing between the two?
faq.a: Architecture, high availability, scoping, security and hybrid environments, to decide between Cloud Sync and Entra Connect.

keypoints: Everyone wants Copilot and AI agents, but fragmented data, conflicting business definitions, weak governance and semantic models not built for AI undermine trustworthy answers.
Walter Calcagno argues that successful enterprise AI starts long before the first prompt.
Organizations need better answers to business questions, not more dashboards, and should start with the decisions they need to make rather than a technology.
Analytics progresses from what happened and why, to what will happen and what actions influence the outcome.
Microsoft Fabric brings storage, movement, analytics, Power BI, Spark and machine learning into one SaaS data platform, with OneLake as a major part.
Walter's path went from accounting and spreadsheets to SQL, Power BI, big data, Spark and AI, and he creates Spanish-language technical content.

faq.q: Why is data readiness important for Copilot?
faq.a: Copilot and agents are expected to give trustworthy answers from enterprise data. If data is fragmented, definitions conflict, governance is weak and semantic models were not designed for AI, the answers cannot be trusted.

faq.q: Should analytics projects start with a technology?
faq.a: No. Walter Calcagno recommends starting with the decisions the organization needs to make. Products like Power BI, Fabric or Python may change, but the business questions remain.

faq.q: What is Microsoft Fabric according to Walter Calcagno?
faq.a: Microsoft's attempt to bring technologies that were assembled individually into a unified Software-as-a-Service data platform covering storage, movement, analytics, big data, Power BI, Spark and machine learning.

faq.q: What is the progression of analytics questions?
faq.a: Understanding what happened, understanding why, predicting what will happen next and asking which actions can influence the desired outcome.

faq.q: Who is Walter Calcagno?
faq.a: A Microsoft MVP in Data Platform, Microsoft Certified Trainer, data architect, author, educator and co-founder of Data Consultants, who began in accounting.

keypoints: Moving an application to an Azure virtual machine does not make it cloud-native; many Windows applications still expect LDAP, Kerberos, NTLM, domain join, DNS and Group Policy.
Entra ID handles modern cloud authentication such as single sign-on and multi-factor authentication but does not replace every capability of traditional Active Directory.
Keeping Active Directory connected to Azure or running domain controller VMs both bring infrastructure and operational responsibilities.
Microsoft Entra Domain Services provides a managed Windows domain inside an Azure virtual network, with Microsoft operating the domain controllers.
Windows VMs can join the domain, legacy apps can perform LDAP queries and workloads can use Kerberos and NTLM, plus DNS and supported Group Policy.
Organizations consume domain services without managing domain controller infrastructure themselves.

faq.q: What is Microsoft Entra Domain Services?
faq.a: It provides a managed Windows domain inside an Azure virtual network. Microsoft runs the domain controllers while workloads use traditional Active Directory capabilities such as domain join, LDAP, Kerberos and NTLM.

faq.q: Why isn't Entra ID alone always enough?
faq.a: Legacy applications often expect to talk directly to a Windows domain using LDAP and Kerberos instead of modern cloud authentication, and Entra ID does not replace all traditional Active Directory capabilities.

faq.q: What problem does Entra Domain Services solve?
faq.a: It lets older applications moved to Azure keep their domain dependencies without running your own domain controllers.

faq.q: Which capabilities does Entra Domain Services offer?
faq.a: Domain join for Windows VMs, LDAP queries, Kerberos and NTLM authentication, DNS and supported Group Policy capabilities.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to Domain Services?
faq.a: Connect your existing Active Directory to Azure or deploy your own domain controller VMs in Azure, both of which add infrastructure and operational responsibilities.

keypoints: Asks what happens when AI stops being a tool and becomes the team that designs, builds, tests, secures, documents, deploys and maintains software.
Mark Smith, known as NZ365Guy, describes building his own AI software factory with specialized autonomous agents.
He uses OpenCLAW as an AI harness and explains how multiple AI models can work together.
Context engineering is becoming more important than basic prompt engineering.
AI changes the interface to software development: outcomes are communicated through prompts, APIs, MCP interfaces, command-line tools and agents instead of configuration screens.
Mark's career spans about 30 years from IT training through Dynamics CRM, Power Platform and Copilot to AI.

faq.q: What is an AI software factory?
faq.a: In this episode it is Mark Smith's setup of specialized autonomous agents that handle parts of software creation, from designing and building to testing, securing, documenting, deploying and maintaining.

faq.q: What is OpenCLAW in this episode?
faq.a: OpenCLAW is the AI harness Mark Smith uses to run his agents and let multiple AI models work together. It is part of the AI software factory he is building with specialized autonomous agents.

faq.q: Why is context engineering more important than prompt engineering?
faq.a: According to the episode, context engineering is becoming more important than basic prompt engineering as agents and multiple models need the right context to work.

faq.q: How is AI changing low-code development?
faq.a: Mark sees a shift from configuring screens in traditional low-code tools to expressing desired outcomes through prompts, APIs, MCP interfaces, command-line tools and AI agents, calling it AI-first software creation.

faq.q: Who is Mark Smith?
faq.a: A Microsoft MVP widely known as NZ365Guy, with decades of experience in Microsoft technologies, Dynamics 365, Power Platform, Copilot and AI, as well as consulting, training and podcasting.

keypoints: Business Central and Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations are not two steps on the same ERP ladder, so moving later is not a simple upgrade.
Business Central evolved from Dynamics NAV and Finance & Operations from Dynamics AX, built for different organizations and operating models.
Architecture, data models, posting logic, dimensions, account structures and legal-entity concepts differ, so a move is closer to a new ERP implementation.
Data must be extracted from Business Central, transformed into F&O structures, loaded through F&O data management tooling and validated.
Business Central prioritizes simplicity for one entity or a few connected companies, while F&O treats multiple entities, countries, currencies and consolidation as given from day one.
Covers consolidation challenges, Dataverse integration, M&A scenarios, migration costs and process redesign.

faq.q: Can you upgrade from Business Central to Finance & Operations?
faq.a: Not in the sense of a traditional upgrade. The underlying architecture is different, so there is no upgrade button and the move resembles a new ERP implementation.

faq.q: Why are Business Central and F&O different products?
faq.a: Business Central evolved from Dynamics NAV and Finance & Operations from Dynamics AX, created for different organizations, levels of complexity and operating models.

faq.q: What does migrating from Business Central to F&O involve?
faq.a: Extracting data from Business Central, transforming it into F&O's structures, loading it with F&O's data management tooling and extensive validation, each with its own workload and risk.

faq.q: What is Business Central built for?
faq.a: Simplicity: one entity or a small number of connected companies, straightforward financial structures and regional operations, with complexity added only when needed.

faq.q: What is Finance & Operations built for?
faq.a: Enterprise complexity from day one, including multiple legal entities, countries and currencies, enterprise consolidation, sophisticated manufacturing and complex approvals.

keypoints: Many PowerPoint problems come from using the same type of deck for different purposes; a deck read as a PDF should not look like slides supporting a speaker.
Experienced users overlook long-standing features such as alignment and distribution tools, grouping, the Selection Pane and object layers.
The Selection Pane helps with layered objects, grouped elements, maps, diagrams and complicated slides made by someone else.
A corporate template should make it easier to create good presentations, not only enforce brand colors and logos.
Slide Master and layouts are the foundation, including title-only and blank layouts and strong image placeholders; overly restrictive templates get worked around.
Copilot relies on the layouts in the template, so a poorly designed template limits AI-generated slides; SmartArt can also look modern.

faq.q: What PowerPoint features do experienced users overlook?
faq.a: Fiona Walsh names alignment and distribution tools, grouping, the Selection Pane and object layers, features that have existed for years and speed up everyday presentation work.

faq.q: What is the Selection Pane useful for?
faq.a: It helps with layered objects, grouped elements, maps, diagrams and complicated corporate slides, including understanding slides created by someone else.

faq.q: What makes a good corporate PowerPoint template?
faq.a: It builds on Slide Master and flexible layouts, with title-only layouts, blank layouts and strong image placeholders. Overly restrictive templates make users delete placeholders or work around them.

faq.q: How does the template affect Copilot in PowerPoint?
faq.a: Copilot relies heavily on the layouts available in the presentation template, so a poorly designed template directly limits the quality of AI-generated slides.

faq.q: Why do PowerPoint decks often fail?
faq.a: Often not because of PowerPoint itself but because the same kind of deck is used for different purposes, such as a document to be read versus slides supporting a speaker.

keypoints: Digital certificates prove the identity of a device or user without repeatedly sharing passwords; the private key stays protected on the device.
PKI, Public Key Infrastructure, creates certificates, delivers them, renews them before expiry and revokes them when they should no longer be trusted.
A typical architecture has a Root CA establishing trust and an Issuing CA handling day-to-day issuance.
Traditional PKI on Windows Server and Active Directory Certificate Services needs connectors, NDES servers, reverse proxies, firewall rules, backups, patching and monitoring.
Microsoft Cloud PKI is a managed Certificate Authority service inside Intune with Microsoft-hosted Root and Issuing CAs.
Covers SCEP, device authentication, secure Wi-Fi and VPN access, renewal and revocation.

faq.q: What is Microsoft Cloud PKI?
faq.a: It is Microsoft's managed Certificate Authority service inside Intune. Organizations use Microsoft-hosted Root and Issuing CAs to issue, renew and revoke certificates for Intune-managed users and devices.

faq.q: Why do devices need certificates?
faq.a: Certificates prove identity without repeatedly sharing passwords. A certificate holds identity information and a public key, while the private key stays on the device, so it can prove possession without exposing the secret.

faq.q: What problem does traditional PKI create for small IT teams?
faq.a: Connecting Intune-managed devices to Active Directory Certificate Services can require connectors, NDES servers, reverse proxies, firewall rules, backups, patching and monitoring, so certificate-based Wi-Fi becomes an infrastructure project.

faq.q: What does a Certificate Authority do?
faq.a: It sits at the center of PKI. A Root CA establishes trust and an Issuing CA handles the daily issuance of certificates.

faq.q: What roles do Entra ID and Intune play with Cloud PKI?
faq.a: Microsoft Entra ID manages identity, while Intune manages company devices, applications and configurations, and hosts the Cloud PKI service.

keypoints: Launching even a simple app involves repositories, Azure subscriptions, networking, identities, secrets, pipelines, monitoring, permissions and several teams.
An Internal Developer Platform is a self-service front door to approved software-building blocks, connecting developers with the organization's automation, standards, tools and policies.
Platform engineering turns cloud infrastructure, security rules, automation and tooling into reusable self-service experiences.
Golden paths are approved, repeatable routes with sensible defaults, where developers provide only service name, owner, environment, runtime and approved options.
Good golden paths also offer controlled escape routes for unusual requirements.
A service catalog maps running software with ownership, documentation, dependencies, code, status and support information; guardrails use Entra ID, Azure Policy and Key Vault.

faq.q: What is an Internal Developer Platform?
faq.a: It is a self-service front door to approved software-building blocks that lets development teams build, deploy and operate applications using the organization's established automation, standards and policies instead of starting from zero.

faq.q: What are golden paths?
faq.a: Approved and repeatable routes for common development tasks. They provide defaults for repositories, CI/CD, Azure resources, identities, monitoring and security, so developers only supply details like service name, owner and runtime.

faq.q: What is a service catalog?
faq.a: A central map of running software with ownership, documentation, dependencies, source code, operational status, dashboards and support information, answering who owns a service and where its code and monitoring are.

faq.q: Does self-service mean unrestricted access?
faq.a: No. Guardrails build organizational requirements into the platform, using Entra ID for access, Azure Policy for resource standards, management groups, Key Vault for secrets and managed identities.

faq.q: What problem do IDPs solve?
faq.a: Developers spend significant time navigating tickets, documentation, portals and infrastructure decisions instead of building features.

keypoints: Every new automation request in Dynamics 365 tends to become a development ticket that waits in a backlog for a developer.
Mirko Peters argues Power Platform should be the visible automation layer between Dynamics 365, Dataverse, people, decisions and connected systems.
This is not an argument against custom code but a framework for where Power Automate, Power Apps, Power Fx, Dataverse, solutions and governance belong.
Asking where to write the code narrows the architecture before the team understands the business change, decision, responders and process owner.
In the traditional model processes spread across plug-ins, JavaScript, workflows, scheduled jobs and integrations, so process owners cannot inspect behavior and support cannot trace failures.
The initial development cost is visible, while the long-term operating cost of custom automation is hidden.

faq.q: Why should Power Platform be the automation layer for Dynamics 365?
faq.a: Because it can interpret signals, apply visible rules, coordinate human decisions, connect services and record what happened between a Dynamics event and the business outcome, instead of burying logic in code.

faq.q: Is the episode against custom code?
faq.a: No. Custom code remains valuable and professional development is still the right choice in some cases, but it should not automatically own every process change.

faq.q: What is wrong with the traditional Dynamics customization model?
faq.a: Each difference becomes another plug-in, script, workflow activity, scheduled job or integration service, so the process is spread across components and specialist knowledge, and nobody truly owns it.

faq.q: What is the hidden cost of custom automation?
faq.a: Initial development appears in estimates and budgets, but the long-term operating cost of maintaining and supporting the custom components is less visible.

faq.q: Which Power Platform elements does the episode discuss?
faq.a: Power Automate, Power Apps, Power Fx, Dataverse, solutions, environment variables, security and governance.

keypoints: Power Platform lets people across an organization build apps and automations quickly, raising questions of who can build what and where company data goes.
Governance should protect the organization without becoming the department that says no, while preventing shadow IT.
The conversation covers security, Data Loss Prevention policies, environment architecture, inventory, application lifecycle management and citizen development.
Michael Roth moved from organizational development and change management into Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Power Automate and Power Apps.
To administrators Power Platform is an enterprise application platform needing configuration, security, maintenance, ownership and monitoring.
Building an app quickly does not make it secure, maintainable, scalable or production-ready, and small automations can become business-critical.

faq.q: How can you govern Power Platform without killing innovation?
faq.a: Michael Roth discusses protecting the organization through security, DLP policies, environment architecture, inventory and lifecycle management while staying enabling instead of saying no to every idea.

faq.q: Is Power Platform just a hobby tool?
faq.a: No. Power Apps, Power Automate, Power Pages, Dataverse and Copilot Studio feel like simple SaaS apps to users, but underneath is an enterprise platform that needs ownership, security, monitoring and operations.

faq.q: What happens when small automations become business-critical?
faq.a: A quickly built flow or app is not automatically secure, maintainable, scalable or ready for production, so organizations take on responsibilities once the platform becomes part of their infrastructure.

faq.q: Which governance topics does the episode cover?
faq.a: Security, Data Loss Prevention policies, environments, inventory, application lifecycle management and citizen development.

faq.q: What is Michael Roth's background?
faq.a: A Microsoft MVP who came from organizational development and change management into the Microsoft ecosystem and combines technical platform knowledge with an understanding of people and adoption.

keypoints: Git is a version control system that records the history of a project and replaces folders named final, final-final and use-this-version.
A commit is a deliberate checkpoint; Git does not commit on every save, and you decide when work belongs in the history.
Each commit should contain one clear, related change with a meaningful message like Fix password reset link rather than Updates.
Small, focused commits are easier to review, compare and reverse without affecting unrelated work.
Git runs locally first: commits, comparisons and branches work without internet, while GitHub is an online place to share and review repositories.
Also covers the working directory, staging area, branches, merges and conflicts.

faq.q: What is Git and what is it used for?
faq.a: Git is a version control system that records the history of a project through deliberate checkpoints, so you can review and compare versions and see which files and lines changed.

faq.q: What is a commit in Git?
faq.a: A recorded checkpoint of the project. You decide when a completed piece of work becomes a commit, and each should hold one clear change with a message that explains what happened.

faq.q: What is the difference between Git and GitHub?
faq.a: Git tracks the project and its history on your own computer. GitHub provides an online location where people share and review Git repositories.

faq.q: Does Git work without an internet connection?
faq.a: Yes. Git is local-first, so you can create commits, inspect changes and use branches without an internet connection. Only GitHub, the online place for sharing repositories, needs one, and a personal project can use Git alone.

faq.q: Why write good commit messages?
faq.a: Messages like Fix password reset link give future developers context, while Updates or Various changes make it hard to investigate a problem months later.

keypoints: The Azure Well-Architected Framework (WAF) is a structured decision-making framework, not a product to activate or a certification badge.
It helps teams design, operate and continuously improve Azure workloads that stay secure, reliable, efficient, manageable and financially sustainable.
A workload includes everything needed for a business outcome, such as code, identities, data, Azure resources, monitoring, deployment processes and people.
The Cloud Adoption Framework builds the shared Azure foundation of governance, security, networking, subscriptions, policies and landing zones, while WAF examines one workload at a time.
In the airport analogy the Cloud Adoption Framework prepares the airport and WAF helps one aircraft complete its journey.
The five pillars are Reliability, Security, Cost Optimization, Operational Excellence and Performance Efficiency, and improving one can create compromises in another.

faq.q: What is the Azure Well-Architected Framework?
faq.a: It is a structured decision-making framework for designing and operating Azure workloads, helping teams ask important architectural questions before weaknesses become expensive incidents.

faq.q: What are the five pillars of the Azure Well-Architected Framework?
faq.a: Reliability, Security, Cost Optimization, Operational Excellence and Performance Efficiency. They are interconnected, so improving one can create costs or compromises in another.

faq.q: How is WAF different from the Cloud Adoption Framework?
faq.a: The Cloud Adoption Framework establishes the shared Azure foundation across the company, including governance and landing zones. WAF examines whether one particular workload can achieve its intended outcome.

faq.q: Is the Well-Architected Framework a product or certification?
faq.a: No. It is neither a product you activate nor a certification you earn but a framework for decisions.

faq.q: What counts as a workload?
faq.a: Everything required to produce a business outcome, for a customer portal this includes application code, identities, customer data, Azure resources, monitoring, deployment processes and the people supporting it.

keypoints: The outdated view of Copilot as a simple question-and-answer system is giving way to an orchestration system that decides where to search, evaluates results and takes action.
Traditional RAG converts a question to an embedding, retrieves chunks from a vector database, adds them to the model context and generates an answer.
Traditional RAG is fast, cheap and effective for simple lookups but struggles when the answer spans several systems, such as why an invoice increased.
In Agentic RAG the model takes part in deciding what information is needed and how to obtain it, following the ReAct pattern of Reason, Act, Reason, Act.
The orchestration loop has six stages: query understanding, planning, multi-source retrieval, tool execution, summarization and safety checks.
Covers implications for Microsoft 365, Copilot Studio, Microsoft Graph, Entra, Purview, MCP, governance and enterprise AI strategy.

faq.q: What is Agentic RAG?
faq.a: Agentic RAG changes the role of the language model: instead of only generating an answer at the end of retrieval, it helps decide what information is required and how to get it, iterating with retrievals and tool calls.

faq.q: How does traditional RAG work?
faq.a: A question is turned into an embedding, relevant chunks are retrieved from a vector database, placed in the model's context and the LLM generates an answer. It works well for finding a policy or a specific fact.

faq.q: Why does single-shot retrieval fail for some questions?
faq.a: When the answer is spread across several systems, one retrieval against one source cannot assemble the picture. Explaining an invoice increase might need current and previous invoices, usage data and pricing terms.

faq.q: What is the ReAct pattern?
faq.a: Reason, Act, Reason, Act: the system analyzes a problem, performs a retrieval or tool call, evaluates the result and decides whether another action is needed, creating an iterative, self-correcting process.

faq.q: What are the stages of the agentic orchestration loop?
faq.a: Query understanding, planning, multi-source retrieval, tool execution, summarization and safety checks.

keypoints: The gap between a chatbot demo and a production-ready agent is much larger than it first appears.
An enterprise agent needs a clear purpose, reliable data, carefully scoped tools, sensible fallback paths and a way for people to understand what it does.
Elliot Margot says organizations should not wait for a perfect governance model but also should not deploy AI blindly; learn by building small, useful solutions.
Governance is a journey, not a blocker, using Data Loss Prevention policies and sensitivity labels, with ownership and continuous learning.
Executive sponsorship works better with service improvement and less repetitive work, such as fewer Level 1 IT tickets, than with headcount promises.
Specialised agents in a multi-agent approach, for example for creating content, reviewing quality or orchestrating workflows, deliver more reliable results than one general agent.

faq.q: What does it take to move an AI agent from demo to production?
faq.a: A clear purpose, reliable data, carefully scoped tools, sensible fallback paths and visibility into what the agent does, plus improving guardrails, monitoring and operating models over time.

faq.q: Should organizations wait for perfect AI governance before starting?
faq.a: No. Elliot Margot recommends establishing foundations, understanding where data goes, applying DLP policies and sensitivity labels, and learning from real usage while continuing to build.

faq.q: How should AI projects be sold to executives?
faq.a: Through real business value such as better service, less repetitive work and more time for judgement-based work, e.g. a modest reduction in repetitive Level 1 IT tickets, combined with a convincing wow moment.

faq.q: Why use multi-agent systems?
faq.a: A single general-purpose agent can try many tasks, but specialised agents with distinct roles, like creating content, reviewing quality or validating requirements, can deliver more reliable results.

faq.q: Who is Elliot Margot?
